when were you born? phrase

also when is your birthday?, what day were you born?, what month were you born in?, date of birth, birth date

modern

Traupman 76

Quandō nātus (nāta) es?

The words and the construction are classical (the ablative of time with nātus, as in sī hic prīdiē nātus foret, Plaut. Mil. 4.2.91, Lewis & Short s.v. prīdiē), but we have found the question itself only in Traupman. The answer gives the day as an ordinal in the ablative: tertiō diē mēnsis Jānuāriī, on the third of January.

Other words

  • Quō diē (Quō mēnse) nātus es? — what day (what month) were you born?

    also used · modern · Traupman 74

Examples

  • Quō diē nāta es? — Quīntō diē mēnsis Majī.

    What day were you born? — On the fifth of May.Traupman 74

  • Tertiō diē mēnsis Jānuāriī.

    On the third of January.Traupman 76

See also birthday, be born, how old are you?, what’s the date?.

SourcesLewis & Short: nascor · Lewis & Short: quando

John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 74, 76.
